A.explanation: All points between two adjacent nodes vibrate in phase and pass through zero displacement together, so the string is momentarily straight and horizontal twice per cycle.

B.explanation: Amplitude varies with position between nodes, being zero at a node and maximum $x_0$ at the antinode, so points do not share the same amplitude.

C.explanation: A string fixed at both ends has a node at each end, so for $n$ loops there are $n+1$ nodes and $n$ antinodes.

D.explanation: Loops on opposite sides of a node move in opposite directions, so adjacent antinodes oscillate in antiphase with phase difference $\pi$ rad.

hints: Notice the string is fixed at both ends, so both ends must always be nodes of zero displacement.
Recall that all points between two adjacent nodes in a stationary wave vibrate in phase but with amplitude that grows from zero at the node to maximum at the antinode.
Think about the instant in the cycle when the time-dependent factor is zero and what the displacement $y$ is for every point at that instant.
walkthrough: Identify the boundary conditions: the two fixed points cannot move, so they are nodes with displacement $y = 0$ at all times.

Recall the stationary wave rule: points between two adjacent nodes all oscillate in phase with the same frequency, but their vibration amplitude depends on position, from $0$ at the nodes to maximum at the antinode.
Write the displacement as position envelope times time oscillation, so at the times when the time factor is zero every point has $y = 0$ simultaneously.
Conclude that the whole loop between the nodes is then straight along the equilibrium horizontal line with zero displacement everywhere.
Contrast this with the other ideas: amplitude is not uniform, nodes exceed antinodes by one, and adjacent loops are in antiphase. This is option A.
